knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Pausing and rerouting keeps people safe. A sign alone does not stop entry.
A sign warns. A barrier or supervision controls access.
Occupied areas change, so the assessment is repeated.

practicalCriteria: Assesses a mock occupied corridor before starting, including exits and accessible paths.
Uses barriers and supervision, not signs alone, at the access point.
Pauses and reroutes when a simulated occupancy change occurs, and reopens only when safe.
passRule: Zone assessed, accessible paths kept open, and occupancy change met by pausing and rerouting. Observed by an assessor.
stopWorkCriteria: Area reopened while the floor is unsafe
